linkedin.caption:
10 selected citizenship routes: Sao Tome and Principe's USD 90,000 donation, Turkiye's USD 400,000 property and Jordan's JOD 350,000 existing-business test. One main applicant; fees extra, eligibility and approval required.

1. Dominica: USD 200,000 to the Economic Diversification Fund. Antigua and Barbuda: USD 230,000 to the National Development Fund. Both use agent-submitted applications; these are contributions, not property purchases.

2. Grenada: USD 235,000 to the National Transformation Fund. Saint Lucia: USD 240,000 to the National Economic Fund, plus a sworn declaration of at least USD 350,000 in financial resources.

3. Saint Kitts and Nevis: USD 250,000 Sustainable Island State Contribution. Turkiye: USD 400,000 qualifying real estate, with a 3-year resale restriction and a presidential citizenship decision.

4. Sao Tome and Principe: USD 90,000 National Transformation Fund donation. Nauru: USD 115,000 regular Treasury contribution; USD 90,000 offer for applications filed before December 31, 2026. Both add fees.

5. Egypt: USD 250,000 Treasury grant. Jordan, outside Capital Governorate: your eligible asset share must average at least JOD 350,000 over 3 audited years, with 10 Jordanian employees on average and at least 9 each month.

Five roles, identical inputs. Unretouched crops from the real salary calculator, rendered locally. Labels distinguish model estimates from observed salaries. Annual USD model estimates · 2 years; North America · Series A/B · 11-50 staff; Security Auditor; Smart Contract Developer; Product Manager; Technical Writer; Community Manager; Auditor minus Community: USD 70,000/year. Model only; tokens/equity excluded. Screenshot text: $133,000; $101,000; $95,000; $76,000; $63,000

linkedin.caption:
At 2 years, North America, Series A/B and 11-50 staff, the calculator estimates Smart Contract Developer salary at USD 101,000/year. Model output, not observed pay. Tokens and equity are outside this estimate.

1. Security Auditor: USD 133,000/year with the same inputs. The model starts at USD 105,000, multiplies by 1.10 for experience and 1.15 for region, then rounds the result to the nearest USD 1,000.

2. Product Manager: USD 95,000/year in the model at 2 years, North America, Series A/B and 11-50 staff. Its USD 75,000 starting value becomes USD 94,875 before rounding.

3. Technical Writer: USD 76,000/year with those same settings. The model calculates USD 60,000 x 1.10 x 1.15 = USD 75,900 before rounding. Company stage and size each contribute a 1.0 multiplier here.

4. Community Manager: USD 63,000/year at the same 2-year settings. The model's USD 50,000 starting value becomes USD 63,250 before rounding. These five results compare the calculator's assumptions, not employer offers.

5. The model puts Security Auditor at USD 133,000/year and Community Manager at USD 63,000/year: a USD 70,000 gap under identical settings. Reproduce the comparison by changing only Primary Role.

Full resource: hashtagweb3.com/salary-calculator/li

linkedin.caption:
Oct 20, 2026 remote Web3 catalog: top 5 explicit-country markets. A historical snapshot, not a claim these vacancies remain open. Most roles were country-restricted; multi-country rows count once per named country.

1. United States: 155 fully remote listings across 30 employers, the largest explicit-country count in the Oct 20 catalog. Eligibility comes from the role's stated location, not the employer's headquarters.

2. United Kingdom: 29 listings across 4 employers. In the Oct 20 catalog, the US had 126 more listings and 26 more employers. This is a comparison of explicitly eligible locations, not company headquarters.

3. Cyprus: 11 listings across 2 employers. Cyprus, Georgia and Poland tie on listing count in the Oct 20 catalog, but their employer counts differ: 2, 1 and 4 respectively.

4. Georgia: 11 listings, all from 1 employer in the Oct 20 catalog. Poland had the same listing count across 4 employers. Equal listing volume can hide very different employer concentration.

5. Poland: 11 listings across 4 employers in the Oct 20, 2026 catalog. Ranking excludes 6 worldwide and 180 unresolved-location listings. Multi-country listings count in each named country, so country totals overlap.

Full resource: hashtagweb3.com/jobs/li

linkedin.caption:
The quiz has four archetypes. One match is The Builder -> Smart Contract Developer: writes on-chain dApp logic. Example practice output: a local deposit/withdrawal contract with tests.

1. The Strategist -> Web3 Product Manager. The quiz describes work on a decentralized product's vision and roadmap. Example practice output: a wallet-onboarding spec covering connection, wrong-network and failed-transaction screens.

2. The Analyst -> On-Chain Data Analyst. The quiz names Dune as a tool for analyzing blockchain data. Example practice output: a query counting daily active wallets, with the chain, time window and wallet definition stated.

3. The Community Weaver -> Community Manager. The quiz describes managing Discord; it also recommends Marketing / Growth Lead and DevRel. Example practice output: a support queue with issue category, escalation owner and resolution note.

4. A fifth role match is The Builder -> Frontend/Web3 Developer, which builds dApp interfaces. Example practice output: a token-balance screen with disconnected, loading and RPC-error states. This shares an archetype with contract development.

5. The Builder result recommends Smart Contract Developer, Frontend/Web3 Developer and Protocol Engineer. Answer 16 questions to see your archetype and its three suggested roles.

Persistent, writable temporary, read-only. Original question screenshot from the live interview bank, followed by a separate authored answer summary. Illustrative modifier fragment; modifier onlyOwner() {;   require(msg.sender == owner);;   _;; }; The caller check runs before the function body.; _; runs the body; code after it runs afterward.; The example assumes owner is defined and initialized; it is a modifier fragment, not a complete ownership contract. Screenshot text: SOL-F-02; Foundation; Knowledge; What is a function modifier and can you provide a simple example?

Read-only does not mean zero computation. Original question screenshot from the live interview bank, followed by a separate authored answer summary. Answer summary · authored; view may read state but cannot modify it. pure may neither read nor modify state. An off-chain eth_call pays no network fee; execution inside a transaction still consumes gas. Screenshot text: SOL-F-04; Foundation; Knowledge; What is the purpose of `view` and `pure` functions?

Answer summary · authored; Implementation code uses the proxy's storage and address, preserving msg.sender and msg.value. Upgrades change the implementation pointer; storage layout must stay compatible. Screenshot text: SOL-I-02; Intermediate; Architecture; What is an upgradeability proxy pattern, and how does `delegatecall` enable it?

linkedin.caption:
A view function can still cost gas, and a packed struct can still cost more to update.
Five Solidity interview questions from our bank, with short answers for the EVM and Solidity 0.8.x.

1. Q: How do storage, memory and calldata differ?
A: storage persists between calls. memory is writable scratch space for a call. calldata is read-only argument data. Use calldata for reference-type inputs you do not need to modify.

2. Q: What is a modifier? Give an example.
A: Reusable logic around a function body. onlyOwner can run require(msg.sender == owner) before _;. The _; placeholder runs the body; code after it runs afterward.

3. Q: What are view and pure for?
A: view may read state but cannot modify it. pure may neither read nor modify state. An off-chain eth_call pays no network fee; execution inside a transaction still consumes gas.

4. Q: How does delegatecall enable an upgradeable proxy?
A: Implementation code uses the proxy's storage and address, preserving msg.sender and msg.value. Upgrades change the implementation pointer; storage layout must stay compatible.

5. Q: How should you order struct fields for storage packing?
A: Group fields that fit in 32 bytes. uint128, uint128, uint256 uses 2 slots; uint128, uint256, uint128 uses 3. Fewer slots do not guarantee cheaper writes.

linkedin.caption:
Malaysia offers Indian tourists 30 visa-free days; Kazakhstan offers 14 per visit. Here are five destinations with the actual limits and entry documents, checked October 20, 2026. Scope: ordinary Indian passports and tourism.

1. Malaysia: up to 30 visa-free days for Indian tourists, under the exemption ending December 31, 2026. Bring a passport valid 6 months, confirmed return ticket and hotel booking; submit the Malaysia Digital Arrival Card before arrival.

2. Thailand: Indian passports get 30 visa-free tourist days under the September 15, 2026 rules, limited to 2 entries per calendar year. Submit TDAC within 3 days before arrival; bring accommodation, onward travel and THB 20,000 per person.

3. Kazakhstan: Indian ordinary passports get up to 14 visa-free days per entry, with a total cap of 42 days in any 180-day period. That makes a 2-week visit possible; leaving and returning does not reset the 42-day allowance.

4. Philippines: 14 visa-free days for Indian tourists, non-extendable and non-convertible. Bring hotel, funds and onward/return proof; passport valid 6 months beyond the stay. Transit-only trips still require a transit visa.

5. Mauritius lists Indian passports as 'No visa required.' Tourist stays can total up to 6 months per calendar year, subject to border approval. Bring return ticket, confirmed stay and funds; passport must outlast the stay.

Full resource: hashtagweb3.com/visas/li

linkedin.caption:
Displaying 1000000 as a token balance can be a million-fold mistake. For a 6-decimal token, that is 1 token.
Five frontend dApp interview questions on reads, units, pending transactions, NFTs and signing, with short answers.

1. Q: What does a provider do in ethers or viem?
A: In ethers v6, a Provider reads chain data; a Signer authorizes transactions. In viem, Public Client exposes reads and Wallet Client handles signing via a wallet or local account.

2. Q: How do you display a uint256 token balance?
A: Use formatUnits(balance, decimals), keeping balance as bigint. In viem, formatUnits(1000000n, 6) returns '1'. Get decimals for that token and chain; never assume 18.

3. Q: Why is an Ethereum transaction stuck, and what should the UI do?
A: Low fees or an earlier pending nonce can block it. Show pending status. A speed-up uses the same nonce with higher fees; cancellation is a competing replacement, not a guarantee.

4. Q: How do you show a wallet's NFTs across contracts?
A: Query an ownership indexer by wallet and chain, paginate results, then render token IDs, metadata and images. Handle missing media. A balanceOf call cannot list every collection.

5. Q: Why use EIP-712 rather than personal_sign for orders?
A: It signs typed fields with a domain, so wallets can show structured terms. Include chainId and verifyingContract. The app must still enforce nonces and expiry.

Full resource: hashtagweb3.com/interview-questions/li

linkedin.caption:
Japan's nomad visa allows 6 months; Thailand's DTV is valid for 5 years but gives 180 days per entry. Five verified remote-work routes below, with their money tests and worker categories. Eligibility varies by nationality and application location.

1. Thailand DTV: 5-year multiple-entry visa; 180 days per entry. Remote workers/freelancers need work evidence and THB 500,000 in funds. London's checklist also requires permanent-residence proof and police clearance.

2. Malaysia's DE Rantau pass: 3-12 months, up to 24 with renewal. Tech freelancers/remote employees need USD 24,000 annual income; non-tech talent needs USD 60,000. Coverage is Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan.

3. Japan's Digital Nomad visa: 6 months, no extension. Remote workers need JPY 10 million annual income and JPY 10 million medical cover. The principal-applicant nationality list includes the US; India is not listed.

4. Costa Rica's remote-worker Estancia lasts 1 year, renewable once. Show USD 3,000/month from overseas work for the previous year (USD 4,000 with dependants), plus USD 50,000 medical cover for the full stay.

5. Barbados Welcome Stamp: 12 months of remote work for overseas clients or employers. Expected income: at least USD 50,000 over that year. Fee after approval: USD 2,000 individual or USD 3,000 family.

Full resource: hashtagweb3.com/visas/li

linkedin.caption:
Dominica can require a 3-year property hold; Saint Kitts and Nevis requires 7. Here are five Caribbean citizenship routes compared by family contribution and asset conditions. USD base amounts; fees and approval checks are additional.

1. Dominica: EDF contribution is USD 200,000 alone or USD 250,000 for the applicant + 3 qualifying dependants. Approved property starts at USD 200,000; hold 3 years from citizenship, or 5 before resale to another CBI applicant.

2. Antigua and Barbuda: USD 230,000 NDF covers a family of up to 4, plus fees. Approved property starts at USD 300,000, held for 5 years after purchase unless replaced with another officially approved property.

3. Grenada: USD 235,000 NTF for up to 4 people; siblings and parents/grandparents 55 or younger cost extra. Qualifying tourism shares start at USD 270,000 plus USD 50,000; 5 years before resale to another CBI applicant.

4. Saint Kitts and Nevis: USD 250,000 SISC covers one applicant or a family of up to 4. Additional dependants add USD 25,000 under 18 or USD 50,000 at 18+. Approved developer property starts at USD 325,000 with a 7-year hold.

5. Saint Lucia: USD 240,000 NEF for applicant + up to 3 qualifying dependants. Alternative: USD 300,000 National Action Bonds held 5 years without interest, plus USD 50,000 administration; other fees extra.

Full resource: hashtagweb3.com/citizenship/li

threads.title: Five smart-contract security questions with concrete answers

sourceImages.alt: Five security questions, answered. Original question screenshot from the live interview bank, followed by a separate authored answer summary. Smart Contract Auditor · EVM · Concrete failure modes; Answer summary · authored; Signature validity alone does not make an action one-use. Enforce a consumed nonce and the correct signing domain. Screenshot text: AUD-I-02; Intermediate; Knowledge; What is a signature replay attack and how can it be prevented?

Slither reports patterns to investigate. Original question screenshot from the live interview bank, followed by a separate authored answer summary. Answer summary · authored; A static analyzer for Solidity and Vyper. It flags patterns such as reentrancy, tx.origin authorization and unchecked calls. Findings need triage; a clean run does not prove safety. Screenshot text: AUD-F-02; Foundation; Knowledge; What is"slither" and what kind of issues can it find?

Credit what the contract receives. Original question screenshot from the live interview bank, followed by a separate authored answer summary. Answer summary · authored; Transfer fees and rebases. For a supported fee-on-transfer token, credit the received balance delta, not the requested amount. Rebases need separate accounting or explicit rejection.; The balance-delta pattern assumes compatible token behavior and safe call handling; it is not universal support for arbitrary tokens. Screenshot text: AUD-I-01; Intermediate; Debugging; You are auditing a simple staking contract. What is the first thing you check for regarding the ERC-20 token being staked?

Validity, domain, nonce, deadline. Original question screenshot from the live interview bank, followed by a separate authored answer summary. Answer summary · authored; Reusing a valid signed action. Sign and consume a nonce, bind the domain to chainId and verifyingContract, and enforce a deadline. EIP-712 alone does not prevent reuse. Screenshot text: AUD-I-02; Intermediate; Knowledge; What is a signature replay attack and how can it be prevented?

Fuzzing a custody vault. Original question screenshot from the live interview bank, followed by a separate authored answer summary. Answer summary · authored; Generated inputs search for broken properties. Echidna can fuzz call sequences; Foundry supports fuzz and invariant tests. Example for a simple custody vault: assets must cover recorded liabilities.; Passing a finite campaign is not proof of correctness; results depend on the property, harness, inputs and explored state. Screenshot text: AUD-A-02; Advanced; Practical; What is fuzzing (or property-based testing) in the context of smart contracts? Name a tool used for it.

A free read still has execution limits. Original question screenshot from the live interview bank, followed by a separate authored answer summary. Answer summary · authored; eth_call still executes on an RPC node and can hit gas caps or timeouts. A getAllOwners() that grows forever can fail. Return bounded pages instead. Screenshot text: AUD-E-02; Expert; Architecture; Describe how"unbounded loops" in view functions can become a vector for a Denial of Service (DoS) attack, even if they don't consume transaction gas.

linkedin.caption:
A valid signature can be reused, and a token can transfer less than the amount requested.
Five smart-contract security interview questions with answers about tools, accounting, replay, fuzzing and read-call limits.

1. Q: What is Slither, and what can it find?
A: A static analyzer for Solidity and Vyper. It flags patterns such as reentrancy, tx.origin authorization and unchecked calls. Findings need triage; a clean run does not prove safety.

2. Q: What token behavior do you check first in a staking audit?
A: Transfer fees and rebases. For a supported fee-on-transfer token, credit the received balance delta, not the requested amount. Rebases need separate accounting or explicit rejection.

3. Q: What is signature replay, and how do you stop it?
A: Reusing a valid signed action. Sign and consume a nonce, bind the domain to chainId and verifyingContract, and enforce a deadline. EIP-712 alone does not prevent reuse.

4. Q: What is fuzzing, and which tool supports it?
A: Generated inputs search for broken properties. Echidna can fuzz call sequences; Foundry supports fuzz and invariant tests. Example for a simple custody vault: assets must cover recorded liabilities.

5. Q: Can an unbounded view loop cause denial of service?
A: Yes. eth_call still executes on an RPC node and can hit gas caps or timeouts. A getAllOwners() that grows forever can fail. Return bounded pages instead.

Full resource: hashtagweb3.com/interview-questions/li

4. Q: What is fuzzing, and which tool supports it?
A: Generated inputs search for broken properties. Echidna can fuzz call sequences; Foundry supports fuzz and invariant tests. Example for a simple custody vault: assets must cover recorded liabilities.

5. Q: Can an unbounded view loop cause denial of service?
A: Yes. eth_call still executes on an RPC node and can hit gas caps or timeouts. A getAllOwners() that grows forever can fail. Return bounded pages instead.

linkedin.caption:
Junior = 1 year; senior = 7 in this example. North America, Series A/B, 11-50 staff throughout. Smart Contract Developer: USD 97,000 vs 124,000/year. These are model salary estimates, excluding tokens/equity, not observed pay.

1. Security Auditor: USD 127,000/year at 1 year versus USD 163,000/year at 7 years. The model difference is USD 36,000/year with North America, Series A/B and 11-50 employees unchanged.

2. Product Manager: USD 91,000/year at 1 year versus USD 116,000/year at 7. The USD 25,000 model difference comes only from the experience input; region, company stage and size stay fixed.

3. Technical Writer: USD 72,000/year at 1 year versus USD 93,000/year at 7. Before rounding, the same model gives USD 72,450 and USD 93,150. The displayed gap is USD 21,000/year.

4. Community Manager: USD 60,000/year at 1 year versus USD 78,000/year at 7. That's a USD 18,000 model difference. These are experience scenarios, not a promise that six more years produces that pay rise.

5. Under the shared inputs, the 1-to-7-year model gap is USD 36,000/year for Security Auditor and USD 18,000 for Community Manager. Set your years, region, company stage and size to compare estimates.

linkedin.caption:
US passport: Japan allows 90-day visa-exempt visits; Thailand now allows 30. Five tourist destinations below, with stay limits and documents. The UK's waiver still requires an ETA. Rules checked October 20, 2026.

1. Japan: US citizens receive 90 days under the short-stay visa exemption. MOFA limits this to visits without income-earning activities. A sightseeing trip fits this route; paid work needs the appropriate immigration status.

2. Taiwan: US citizens get up to 90 visa-free days, counted from the day after arrival. Your US passport must cover the stay; carry confirmed return/onward travel and submit the Taiwan Arrival Card within 7 days before arrival.

3. Canada: US citizens need neither a visitor visa nor an eTA. Visits are usually allowed for up to 6 months; the border officer can set a different end date. Travel with a valid US passport, and follow any date on the entry record.

4. United Kingdom: US tourists can visit visa-free for up to 6 months, but normally need an ETA before travel. The current ETA fee is GBP 20. Passport must cover the whole stay; show funds and plans to leave after the visit.

5. Thailand: US tourists get 30 visa-free days; max 2 exemption entries per calendar year. Free TDAC: within 3 days before arrival. Bring accommodation, onward-travel proof and THB 20,000/person or THB 40,000/family.

linkedin.caption:
The quiz recommends Smart Contract Developer for The Builder, On-Chain Data Analyst for The Analyst, and Community Manager for The Community Weaver. Example outputs: a contract, a query and a support runbook.

1. Builder practice task: implement a local escrow's deposit and withdrawal functions. Deliver the Solidity file, Foundry tests for unauthorized and repeat withdrawals, and a README with the test command. This is a proposed exercise.

2. Analyst practice task: count distinct tx.from addresses per UTC day for one DEX over 30 days. Deliver SQL, chain/contract filters and a chart. Count repeat swaps once per address/day; label transaction senders, not users.

3. Community Weaver practice task: draft a mock support runbook. Example entry: wallet won't connect; category = connection; owner = support moderator; next step = collect browser, wallet version and error text. Output: queue plus handoff note.

4. Security research sits under The Analyst too: Smart Contract Auditor is one of its recommended roles. A practice output could be a short finding with the failing test, affected function and proposed fix.

5. The Analyst result suggests On-Chain Data Analyst, Smart Contract Auditor and Quantitative Analyst. Take the 16-question quiz for your role list, then choose a practice task; the exercises above are our examples.

Full resource: hashtagweb3.com/web3-career-quiz/li

linkedin.caption:
Five-city December shortlist: monthly mean >=25 C, rain <=80 mm, estimated cost <=USD 1,300. Ordered by rainfall. Climate references from the directory, not a December 2026 forecast.

1. Lagos, Nigeria: December reference mean 27.6 C, 11 mm rain and 75% humidity. Estimated cost: USD 1,100/month. The tradeoff: its site safety rating is 4/10, despite meeting this weather-and-budget filter.

2. Bangkok, Thailand: December reference mean 27 C, 18 mm rain and 62% humidity. Estimated cost: USD 1,100/month. Same budget as Lagos, with 13 percentage points lower reference humidity.

3. Siem Reap, Cambodia: December reference mean 25.3 C, 33 mm rain and 72% humidity. Estimated cost: USD 800/month, including USD 280 rent. It has the lowest budget in this five-city shortlist.

4. Cartagena, Colombia: December reference mean 27.5 C, 34 mm rain and 80% humidity. Estimated cost: USD 1,300/month. Rain is only 1 mm above Siem Reap's reference, but the budget is USD 500 higher.

5. Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam: December reference mean 26.7 C, 64 mm rain and 77% humidity. Estimated cost: USD 1,000/month. That is USD 100 below Bangkok, with 46 mm more reference rainfall.

2. EthCC[10] | Apr 12-15, 2027 | Cannes, France. Palais des Festivals hosts the four-day Ethereum community conference. Full passes cover all 4 days; student and volunteer access options are listed.

linkedin.caption:
Practice rewrite for a technical resume: 'Built a dApp' becomes 'Built a React token-balance view with disconnected, loading and RPC-error states.' Put it in the project's Description field. Example wording.

1. Community practice rewrite: 'Managed Discord' becomes 'Drafted a mock support queue with issue category, escalation owner and resolution note.' Your Role: Personal practice project. This describes a sample artifact, not past employment.

2. Content practice rewrite: 'Wrote about crypto' becomes 'Wrote a practice guide explaining approve and transferFrom with a worked allowance example.' Project Name: Sample Token Approval Guide. This is example wording, not a published article claim.

3. Example summaries connect each target to its sample: frontend developer building a balance view; community contributor drafting a support queue; content writer explaining token approvals. Put the sentence in Professional Summary.

4. The technical example gives an interview walkthrough: disconnect the wallet, load a balance, then simulate an RPC error. The community example gives a support walkthrough: classify, assign, record the resolution. These are practice prompts.

5. In the builder, use Key Projects & Portfolio for these practice pieces. Project Name, Your Role, Description and Link are separate fields; Download PDF exports the preview.

Full resource: hashtagweb3.com/resume-builder/li

linkedin.caption:
For an Indian passport, Nepal is visa-free, Indonesia sells a 30-day visa on arrival, and Vietnam offers an advance eVisa. Here are five named examples with the documents, fees or conditions that distinguish them. Tourist travel, checked October 20.

1. Nepal: Indian nationals do not need a visa. Carry a valid Indian passport or Election Commission voter card. Nepal Tourism Board explicitly says Aadhaar is not an accepted travel document; a domestic ID is not automatically border ID.

2. Bhutan: Indian visitors need an entry permit, not a visa. For a 5-night inland trip, adult SDF is INR 6,000 (INR 1,200/night), before accommodation and the mandatory guide. Carry an Indian passport or voter ID.

3. Maldives: tourist visa issued on arrival, rather than visa-free entry. Bring an MRZ passport valid at least 1 month, prepaid registered accommodation and return ticket. Submit the free IMUGA traveller declaration within 96 hours before arrival.

4. Indonesia: Indian passports qualify for B1 visa on arrival, IDR 500,000 for up to 30 days. One extension can bring the total to 60 days. Carry a passport valid at least 6 months and onward/return ticket. Online e-VOA is also available.

5. Vietnam: Indian tourists can apply in advance for an eVisa of up to 90 days. USD 25 single-entry or USD 50 multiple-entry; no refund if refused. Follow the granted dates and use designated eVisa border gates.

Full resource: hashtagweb3.com/visas/li

linkedin.caption:
A wallet signature proves account control, not legal identity. Active wallet counts also do not count people.
Five courses in our learning library, with a named lesson and a concrete takeaway from each.

1. Web3 Fundamentals (15 lessons): Wallets and Private Keys.
A wallet signs messages and transactions. In self-custody, you control keys or permissions; a custodian controls them for you. A signature proves account control, not legal identity.

2. Decentralized Finance (9 lessons): Lending and Borrowing in DeFi.
Example: 80% LTV on $1,000 collateral gives an $800 borrowing cap. Liquidation uses a separate threshold, with parameters set per market.

3. Smart Contract Development (9 lessons): Testing Smart Contracts.
The sample transfers 100 units from a 1,000-unit balance and asserts 100 received, 900 left. Foundry fuzz tests then vary the amount to test properties.

4. Web3 Marketing & Community (8 lessons): Growth Metrics and Analytics.
Unique Active Wallets counts addresses over a defined period. One person can control several. Retention asks how many wallets in a starting cohort return later.

5. AI x Crypto Intersection (7 lessons): Autonomous Agents.
Separate model, tools and wallet. Balance reads should not grant transfer-signing permission. Enforce spending caps and contract allowlists.

Full resource: hashtagweb3.com/learn/li

linkedin.caption:
Dominica's USD 200,000 fund needs USD 210,000 for the contribution + 4 published fees. Five citizenship cost comparisons for one main applicant below. These are itemized subtotals; unlisted professional, document and transaction costs remain extra.

1. Dominica EDF: USD 200,000 + 1,000 processing + 7,500 due diligence + 500 certificate + 1,000 interview = USD 210,000. Agent, passport, bank and any enhanced-check costs remain extra.

2. Antigua and Barbuda NDF: USD 230,000 + 10,000 processing + 8,500 due diligence + 300 passport = USD 248,800 for a single applicant, before agent charges.

3. Sao Tome and Principe: USD 90,000 donation + 5,000 submission + 750 citizenship documents = USD 95,750 before agent costs. Sponsored applications add USD 5,000 benefactor due diligence.

4. Saint Lucia bonds: USD 300,000 capital + 50,000 administration + 2,000 processing + 8,000 due diligence = USD 360,000 before other costs. The bonds earn no interest and must be held 5 years; fees are not bond capital.

5. Egypt: USD 500,000 Central Bank deposit + USD 10,000 non-refundable application fee = USD 510,000 upfront. The deposit is repaid after 3 years in Egyptian pounds at the Central Bank rate on repayment, without interest.

Full resource: hashtagweb3.com/citizenship/li

linkedin.caption:
USD 1,800/month ceiling; site walkability >=7.5/10; 2026 Q1 download >=200 Mbps. Exclude missing walk scores. Top 5 eligible cities, sorted by walkability then download, highest first. Costs are directory estimates.

1. 1. Prague, Czech Republic: site walkability 8.8/10; USD 1,800/month estimated. Fixed broadband: 252.9 down / 153.9 up Mbps (2026 Q1). Highest walk score among cities passing all three filters.

2. 2. Budapest, Hungary: site walkability 8.5/10; USD 1,400/month estimated. Fixed broadband: 344.5 down / 165.3 up Mbps (2026 Q1). It is USD 400 below the ceiling and wins the walk-score tie with Osaka on download.

3. 3. Osaka, Japan: site walkability 8.5/10; USD 1,800/month estimated. Fixed broadband: 210.5 down / 175.2 up Mbps (2026 Q1). It matches Budapest's walk score, with lower download but 9.9 Mbps higher upload.

4. 4. Taipei, Taiwan: site walkability 8/10; USD 1,800/month estimated. Fixed broadband: 259.7 down / 166.8 up Mbps (2026 Q1). The directory also rates transit at 8.8/10.

5. 5. Porto, Portugal: site walkability 7.8/10; USD 1,800/month estimated. Fixed broadband: 359.9 down / 225.5 up Mbps (2026 Q1). Fastest download among these five, but fifth in the walkability-first ranking.
